-   **Rarity note:** Rare species in Florida, found on palmetto and other palm leaves.

## Natural history notes

A crustose lichen characterized by a thin brownish to olive-gray thallus with small dark fruiting structures scattered across the surface. In Florida, it is found growing on palmetto leaves and other palm or bark surfaces in humid habitats such as hammocks, swamps, pine flatwoods, shaded forests, and landscaped areas where palmettos are common. Like other lichens, it is a symbiotic association between a fungus and photosynthetic partner, growing tightly attached to the plant surface and absorbing moisture and nutrients from the air rather than feeding on the plant itself.
